anchor_issues: Row 31, D3: the row spans reclassification (ADA says C-peptide is indicated in insulin-treated people: 3) and insulin discontinuation (ADA says it must be measured first: 4). I scored the primary decision in the row text, 'stop or avoid insulin', as 4 (anchors 7 and 13) and noted the other part.

Row 10, D3: Igls is a consensus statement by international societies, not a guideline or label. C-peptide is a required element of two of the four graft-function categories, but the text says 'should be measured' (pretransplant baseline) and it is one of four criteria. I scored 3; 4 is arguable if a consensus statement that defines the classification counts as requiring the test.

Row 49, D3: the FDA teplizumab label uses C-peptide decline as a surrogate for a second indication (recently diagnosed stage 3, accelerated approval). That is not the decision named in this row (prognosis in stage 1 or 2), so it was not used for D3; D3 for that other use would differ. Row 49 also uses post-load C-peptide, which the project did not evaluate as a predictor.

Row 7, D3: ADA does not name C-peptide in the MODY testing recommendation; ISPAD lists it as one suspicion feature; the ANZ 2025 consensus (non-US national) names a C-peptide-based pathway but was not re-read. Anchor 6 (national criteria) put the ANZ document at 1 for the US; I scored the US/international position as 2.

Row 3, D3: the Endocrine Society recommendation is for evaluating suspected endogenous hyperinsulinism in adults; I counted it as covering the sulfonylurea use case because it lists the oral hypoglycaemic agent screen in the same panel (anchor 14 requires the text to cover the population explicitly). Abstract-level only, so medium confidence.

Rows 31, 47, 49, 3 and 10, D7: anchor 1 requires a share of the existing pool that is evaluated in a year; no source gives these shares, so each is a labelled assumption with its own range. Rule 21 says to record 'bin X or Y' when the bin-deciding share crosses a boundary, but the JSON score must be an integer. I scored the bin of the point estimate (anchor 3) and wrote the alternative bin in the reason and set confidence low.

Row 4, D7: anchor 4 (situations, not diagnoses) was applied to 'persistent hypoglycaemia with a critical sample', which includes older children; no US count of such evaluations exists, so the figure is extrapolated from one Canadian regional review.
Row 32, D7: HCUP-based DKA counts are events (admissions and ED visits), not patients, and the type split is coded type, not C-peptide-based type.
Commonality sources carry different years (CDC 2012 to 2023, SEARCH 2017-2018, HCUP 2014, OPTN 2023-2024); counts for chronic conditions drift upward, so older figures are slight underestimates.
assumptions: Latest available CDC and OPTN figures were used as the current US annual numbers; no inflation to 2026.
Row 31: 3.8 million adults who started insulin within a year of diagnosis stands in for the insulin-treated pool; share evaluated per year 1-5% (assumption).
Row 7: adults aged 20-34 are about 40% of new adult cases in the 20-44 band; 5-10% of them are non-obese and antibody-negative (assumption).
Row 3: 5-10 million US sulfonylurea users; 5-20% of hypoglycaemia events worked up with insulin, C-peptide and drug screen (assumptions; no source).
Row 32: 20% of adult DKA events are new-onset (assumption); ketosis-prone share 35% from the meta-analysis.

Row 47: 10-25% of slowly progressive autoimmune cases are recognised by antibody testing (assumption); C-peptide threshold is the Japanese 0.6 ng/mL fasting value, while US ADA wording uses a random 600 pmol/L cut-off.
Row 49: 10,000-20,000 relatives screened per year by TrialNet and 1,000-5,000 new stage 1-2 identified per year across all channels (assumptions).
Row 4: Manitoba births about 16,500 per year (not sourced) for the extrapolation.
Row 10: prevalent pancreas graft pool 8,000-10,000 and islet numbers are not sourced; shares evaluated are assumptions.
